text:
mira: quick brain dump — proposing a tiny in-band "progress checkpoint" frame for streaming responses so edge can safely resume without duplicating side-effects. idea is lightweight, checksumed, monotonic seq id.

sam: curious — how is this different from existing resume tokens?
mira: resume tokens today are opaque and tied to specific backend state. this would be explicit, client-visible checkpoints emitted periodically by the model layer and passed through the gateway. helps for: retries, migrating long streams between workers, and debugging client-visible progress.

raj: sketch the frame pls, short & backward-compatible?
mira: yep. something like: 
```
PROGRESS_FRAME := {
  version: 1,
  seq: 42,                 // monotonic per-request frame id
  byte_offset: 12345,     // how many response bytes emitted so far
  token_count: 512,       // soft hint for consumption accounting
  crc32: "0x9a1f2b3c"    // checksum of payload up to this point
}
```
kevin: idea: have gateways honor these frames but not require them. if present, gateway stores last seen seq per request and can ask backends to resume from the nearest safe checkpoint. makes it optional for older clients.

mira: exactly. semantics: backend emits frames every N tokens or on sentence boundaries. gateway persists minimal metadata (seq, crc, offset) in memory with a small eviction TTL (e.g. 30s) to avoid disk IO. if worker dies, router can attempt resume on compatible worker using the last checkpoint.

sam: what about side-effects? if the model triggered an external webhook earlier in the stream, resuming might repeat it. we still need idempotency hooks.

raj: we can't solve all side-effects but can reduce dup window. propose combining progress frames with a lightweight server-side idempotency key that maps to externally-observed side-effects; clients/app layer remain responsible for final-safe semantics.

kevin: performance concerns: storing per-stream state in gateway increases memory pressure. we should make it bounded: store only last checkpoint per request, fixed-size entry, and TTL. also expose metrics: checkpoint-emitted-rate, resume-success, resume-fallthrough.

mira: ops-bot FYI: I posted a short RFC in docs (link) with perf sims.
ops-bot: Mira posted: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/stream-checkpointing — auto-notify

sam: one more edge case: partial frames when connection closes mid-frame. recommend CRC be computed over canonicalized payload so receiving component can detect truncated frames and ignore corrupt checkpoints.

raj: agreed. and gating: gateway only attempts resume when backend advertises "resume-capable" and checkpoint version matches. otherwise fallback to full retry or fail-open depending on route policy.

kevin: implementation tasks rough: 1) small wire frame proto + canonical CRC 2) gateway in-memory checkpoint store + TTL 3) backend resume API (accept seq/crc/offset) 4) metrics & rollout flags.

mira: thanks — I'll add an RFC checklist and ping runtime/serving for a sync. short question for arch team: ok to keep TTL default 30s and make it configurable per-route?

sam: +1 to configurable per-route. default 30s seems fine.

raj: +1. let's schedule a 30-min sync if runtime folks want to prototype.

kevin: tagging @runtime-team and @serving for visibility.
